title: Quotient map associated to an intersection-refining open covering
statement: Let $X$ be the underlying topological space of a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal C$ be a collection of open subsets with $X=\bigcup_{U\in\mathcal C}U$ and $U\cap V=\bigcup_{W\in\mathcal C,\,W\subset U\cap V}W$ for all $U,V\in\mathcal C$. Then there are a topological space $Y$ and a continuous map $f:X\to Y$ such that each $f(U)$ is open, $f^{-1}(f(U))=U$ for every $U\in\mathcal C$, and the opens $f(U)$ form a basis for the topology on $Y$. Here continuity means that inverse images of open sets are open, and a basis means a family of opens such that every open of $Y$ is a union of members.

source.place: Tag 0D5Q (topology-lemma-create-map-from-subcollection); specialized to the underlying topological space of a scheme

proof.text: Define an equivalence relation on points of $X$ by $x\sim y$ if and only if, for every $U\in\mathcal C$, one has $x\in U$ exactly when $y\in U$. Let $Y$ be the set of equivalence classes and let $f:X\to Y$ send a point to its class. For every $U\in\mathcal C$, the definition gives $U\subseteq f^{-1}(f(U))$; conversely, if $x\in f^{-1}(f(U))$, then $x\sim y$ for some $y\in U$, so the defining equivalence condition gives $x\in U$. Thus $f^{-1}(f(U))=U$.

source.place: Tag 0D5Q, proof, construction of the equivalence relation and quotient map

proof.text: For $U,V\in\mathcal C$, one has $f(U)\cap f(V)=f(U\cap V)$. Indeed, if a class has representatives $x\in U$ and $y\in V$, then $x\sim y$ implies that $x$ belongs to $V$ and hence to $U\cap V$, so the class lies in $f(U\cap V)$; the reverse inclusion is immediate. The intersection hypothesis on $\mathcal C$ therefore gives $f(U)\cap f(V)=\bigcup_{W\in\mathcal C,\,W\subset U\cap V}f(W)$. Since $X=\bigcup_{U\in\mathcal C}U$, the sets $f(U)$ cover $Y$. Declare the opens of $Y$ to be exactly the unions of these sets $f(U)$. Arbitrary unions are automatic, and the displayed intersection formula shows that finite intersections are again unions of such sets, so this is a topology and the family $\{f(U):U\in\mathcal C\}$ is a basis.

source.place: Tag 0D5Q, proof, identification of intersections and application of Lemma make-base (Tag 0D5P)

proof.text: The map $f$ is continuous: every open subset of $Y$ is a union of basis opens $f(U)$, and its inverse image is the corresponding union of the open subsets $f^{-1}(f(U))=U$ of $X$. This also proves the asserted openness of every $f(U)$ and completes the construction, including empty $X$ or an empty indexing family (where the quotient and the generated topology are empty).
